comment: AMAZING VIEW, inclines are hell
Zero bugs today, dry. Lots of roots and rocks so it's definitely a moderate level. Going to play "Can you eat it?" With all the amazing types of mushrooms along the trails! Great hike!
gorgeous trail with lots to look at, very worth it. definitely a bit technical and a little muddy towards the end of the trail.
Bit of a climb to the lookout (133 stairs!) but the view is worth it!
Beautiful Rivers, lakes and the look out is spectacular!
Gorgeous trail with great views highly recommend. Cautious is very crowded and muddy.

Challenging trail with small rocks and and roots that seem to grab you feet even after you clear them. The stairs were burning my thighs at the end. The lookout was a very rewarding. I 've done the trail twice now and I've changed my evaluation of difficulty from Strenuous to Hard. Near the end of the trail be careful going down the wooden stairs, they are a little wobbly. BTW F*CK PARKINSON'S
Amazing trail with so many varying terraine.  Make sure to wear proper hiking shoes, no sandals.
Pretty crowded at the lookout, nice views
Good hike with nice views throughout! Definitely buggy so bring spray
Lovely walk, not too difficult and lovely view plus lakeside views
Good day hike

Easygoing trail I hiked with a friend.  Mostly rolling hills with only one section following a steady incline up a hill and then stairs.  Great view at the top!

I’d rate this (personally) on the easy side of moderate.
Pretty tough conditions with all the mud on the last half. Also very buggy. Got my monies worth of deet. Views were pretty filled in as it was July and tons of rain this year.
The trail itself is amazing. However the all trails trail says it is 8.4 km when I reality it is 13 with the lookout.
Pretty muddy in some areas sod the trail. Recommend to wear proper footwear
My husband and I and our dog Sophie 🐕 we hiked the trail 👣 today! We have hiked this trail 👣 before and it is a very hard trail! Especially once u get to the stairs!
Muddy but beautiful
Muddy terrain and a lot of mosquitoes. But a very good hike overall. Be prepared with a mosquito net or bug spray.

Amazing hike with awesome sights and views. Terrain gets difficult in places but it’s a very fun hike, and the lookout is worth it, don’t skip! But it is very muddy this time of year and the mosquitoes are bad. Come prepared! You need hiking boots, bug spray, and water! Saw too many people on this trail with little to no water. This trail ended up being 8.7 km.
Bring real bug spray or a mosquito nets and you’ll have a grand ol’ time
Lots of mosquitoes, trail quite muddy
So many mosquitoes when we hike, bring a net cover for your face
Way too many mosquitoes in June
A little wet from the rain
Great trail, unreal view from the top. Variable terrain, lots of wildlife along the way

A bit muddy.  Lots of bugs but bug spray worked.  Great view!
The hike out on the 2nd half of the loop going counterclockwise was not very interesting.  Next time I’d hike out the way I came in to view the river and rapids again.
Girl do NOT go after a rainfall 😭 No amount of bug spray could ward them off- 10/10 trail though the view was incredible!!
There is a broken staircase on the way to the lookout that some might find challenging to get around. Overall a beautiful, varied hike. Best so far in Algonquin
Nice lookout, beautiful lake. Really cool bridge you can see collapsed in the water. Not too many humans which was great. Stairs to lookout was broken by fallen trees. Needs repair
Muddy in the last km
Quite a fun walk. Muddy from time to time. Wonderful view over the area halfway through the walk. Not too exhausting.

First half of the trail is A LOT more interesting including the lookout tower. The last 2 km seemed never ending and pretty boring. Wear good hiking shoes/boots this time of year. View of Cache Lake and the old railway bridge remains were fabulous and worth the trek.
We went after a rainfall mid May, still some part muddy but lots of dry areas and even some cool waterfalls and views of the dam
Need to do loop to get the best view

As an unexperienced hiker the trail was fair! It was a lot of uphill sections & a big set of stairs - definitely a thigh burner! We brought our puppy along with no problem - only recommend to keep on leash due to the beautiful cliff view!
Muddy trail, lots of detours. Up and down with a decent view point, centennial trail more worth it. Old rail was cool though.

Great walk in beginning of the May. Muddy in places but with good boots it feels like a walk in a park. We went to the view point which is worth it. Tho the last leg of the walk felt a bit long as it was nothing much to see (but that might be just us)
Nice view - rushing waters and mud. Trout Lillie’s and trilliums in leaf and bud - only trout Lilly flowers at the top
Lots of fun bridges, wooden boardwalk and beautiful streams and waterfalls
I have done 7 trails at Algonquin Park and this one is my favourite one.

Great trail, not many people, we took the detour to see the lookout and that was great. 
As of April 25, there’s still some ice on the trail but totally manageable, especially with hiking shoes . Some parts are muddy from the melting ice and running water.

A great trail - good conditions for early spring, bit muddy and icy in places but totally fine with good shoes. Definitely longer than the 7.5km advertised, especially going to lookout - we tracked 9km total. But not hard overall, a good climb at the end but a great view - would be wonderful to see it change through the seasons!

As of April 22nd

Still areas with snow and ice. Few fallen trees. Still a very great hike!

Great hiking trail for a weekend. I would recommend this during summer. In winter, the trail is icy and muddy which makes difficult to walk. We came across Moose nearby the parking lot which was the highlight of our hike.
Took about 4 hours because of some snowy and icy parts. Beautiful spots along the lakes, river and on top of the hill.
In the winter months, the ice and snow make it challenging. Great trail overall!
Lots of amazing views along the way! A bit technical and breaking trail a lot but that also means not a lot of people & it was winter!
Difficult with snow conditions but beautiful and worth the extra trip to the lookout if you’re able.. closer to 10km all in.
It was beautiful but it was an extremely difficult hike due to sinking into the snow every other step. Exhausting. We still loved it and loved having it all to our selves today.
Wonderful day. Trail well packed.
Was  well walked however due to the weather (bright sunshine) it meant that the trail was more difficult to walk due to the melting snow! Still a gorgeous hike!
Great trail and very accessible for this time of year. Snowshoes weren’t necessary, but microspikes were a nice bonus for the steeper stretches.
i had the most beautiful time. the stairs were a bit tricky to climb up but the slide down was so fun!
Was amazed at the maintenance of this trail. Groomed well, no snowshoes or picks needed. Snow is well packed down.
The stairs are not snowshoe nor hiking boots friendly.

Trail was packed down, easy to walk without snow shoes or micro spikes though micro spikes were helpful on the stairs. Stairs up to the lookout were a little challenging with the snow but manageable. Expect to take longer than without snow.

The distance can be a little deceiving. I did this hike in the snow and it is much more challenging the snow. There’s some elevations where it become slippery, especially at the part you hit a fork in the trail and to the right is the main highlight lookout there’s a huge flight of stairs and when it’s snow-covered, it’s very difficult to climb and Taxi so just be aware of that fact I wouldn’t recommend it if you have physical restraints.
Recommend snow shoes in winter. Little sketchy on up and downs with out.

Mother nature just took a giant white dump, so you're going to have to be prepared with a pretty unpacked trail (you're welcome) and pretty challenging conditions. If you step off the current thing trail you'll post-hole through 1-2ft of snow, and any downhills can be treacherous so hopefully you also have a fat butt when you inevitably slide onto it lol. The bright side is that it's not icy, so at least you won't need crampons right now. Oh, and also the trail is tons of fun and looks beautiful with all the snow all over it.
Easy trail with a scenic lookout and very accessible in snowy conditions. Completed in 2.5 hrs
Great hike. Would do again.
Wonderful hike, the trail is well marked. No mud because the ground was frozen. So many pretty sights and the lookout is beautiful.
Lovely hike! Lookout view is amazing. Nice and quiet this time of the year too (Nov). Would recommend waterproof shoes as muddy / snowy.
Good trail, lots of view points and points of interest with a really interesting paper guide.
On the easier side, I’d only put it as moderate because of the steep climb to the lookout. Great view. Good trail. Definitely worth it.

Way longer and more difficult than I thought it would be. A lot of uphill and rooted/rocky sections. Decent amount of mud on a day offer some rain, I’d recommend hiking boots. There is a bathroom shortly after the lookout section. Overall it was good but I definitely would have gone for something a little bit easier if I knew how difficult it was. Glad I did it though :)
Really long trail but def fun and led to a nice little peak for the view of Algonquin!

Beautiful trail, variety of forest paths.  Being fall and dry, the trail was hard packed but lots of tree roots to work around, and a moderately strenuous climb for the view.  The lookout point was a little crowded with a tour group when I passed by… and unfortunately as happens in any busy park there was some litter along the way, but overall a beautiful hike.

Really crowded today, but it was thanksgiving. We are unfortunately past the peak fall time (which we barely got this year, thanks climate change) but the bright side is that walking in the forest is really pretty with sunshine and fresh red and orange everywhere along the ground. The trail conditions are the driest I've ever seen, which includes walking in places where waterfalls once were. There is virtually no mud, and the streams barely exist. Blessings and curses and all that. Still the best overall trail on 60 and a ton of fun.
Great.  Got there early and enjoyed it very much!!  Crowded when we left.  But all good!
Long weekend with beautiful weather, so there were a few bottlenecks yhd trail. It was a decent workout, with a couple of viewpoints. Mostly just forest. Happy that we did it once, would not revisit.
Crowded
It took 6hrs cause I did it with my 2yrs old. We got there around 8am and there were only a few cars. But while I was getting ready, cars were keep coming non stop. It's a long weeke

Trail was beautiful, maples have shed quite a bit but the Aspen and Birch were beautiful. The view from the top was underwhelming given the lack of popping colours due to the maples dropping most their leaves. The trail itself was not too crowded and I would rate it as moderate at the most in terms of difficulty.
Nice trail, beautiful views, but crowded
Would recommend good hiking shoes as a lot of leaves have fallen and trails are covered
Great trail, easy to follow. Good views throughout and at the top.

Nice trail with some sections with roots and rock, mostly flat with a few stairs. This is not a hard trail, rather a easy/moderate level. Nice view at the look out, it can be easily too crowded on weekends. Though not challenging, it is one of the nice ones in the park.
Great nice trail. Nice view of the forest and lake. Easy.
Lots of spots for dogs to jump into the water.
First Hike crushed it
beautiful views at the lookout! so worth the hike
Got busy at 11 but empty at 730 am
Beautiful in fall
Carry enough water and food, trail is 4 hours long with many climbs and descends. Watch your steps while walking through woods, take enough breaks and stay hydrated.
A very challenging trail but amazing views from the scenic spot. Weather was great and it was super busy.
The view is awesome

Amazing hike! The trail takes you to different landscapes from forest to lakes to lookout, it was enjoyable the whole way and not that difficult although definitely not accessible. Even if you decide to skip the lookup and just do the loop, you will still enjoy it.

A variety of all the best scenery that Algonquin has to offer. Beautiful vistas, dense forests, lakes, ponds, marshes, boardwalks, hills, and history. A nice balance of walkable trails and more challenging climbs. Not too many people on the trail if you set out before 10:00 am.
Great trail, well marked. Not too crowded even with parking lot full. Be prepared to do stairs for the lookout
Doing the whole loop is very fun and enjoyable. Different view points gave me motivation to keep going. Even while walking through the forest it was very beautiful.

Nice easy hike in Algonquin to see the fall leaves at the end of September
However very crowded on the weekend and otherwise not many viewpoints
It's a 8 km loop. I'd say the most challenging part is the last 1 km where you have to go up the stairs and elevation. Other than that, the rest of the trail is relatively flat or small inclination.
Wonderful trail! It has everything
Popular loop trail in Algonquin Park. Climbs to lookout of Cache Lake. Well marked. Not muddy, but a lot of tree roots to navigate.
Amazing spots
Beautiful trail, super busy this weekend due to leaves changing but people good enough to let pass if needed, and long enough trail you don’t have to be on top of people.
Nice trail and in good condition.  Lots of tree roots and rocks to navigate.  Lookout spots were too busy though.
Easy trail. Great views. Definitely beginner friendly. Fall is the best season to hike cause of the great colours.
Popular trail, very busy at the lookout point
The trail was defiantly up and down most of the way through the woods. Once we got to the lookout it was 100% worth it. The view was amazing!!
We enjoyed stunning, fall colors, both on the trees and on the ground.
Good variety of terrain. There’s one steep section with stairs that will give you a workout, but the view is worth it.
Rocky with tree roots. Not too difficult
Good view going up to the midpoint where lookout is, returning from the lookout is not that exciting as it is long and plan, no scenic points coming down and lots of elevation

Well marked, well maintained trail with some great views! The first part of the trail up to the lookout point was a highlight (we hiked the trail clockwise). The conditions were also dry and there were little to no bugs. Be warned that part of the trail to the lookout is quite steep.

Great trail
Great condition, well marked
Technical trail, great views and atmosphere!
The lookout was brilliant. If you go right... slightly longer then just going right at the top 9f the stairs. Stairs were in great conditions.
Great trail!! A few challenging areas, but take breaks, stay hydrated and fuel yourself!
Excellent trail - excellent views
went on twice just to get a good look at the beautfiul views at post 7.
A wonderful varied trail with wildlife through and a stunning vista!
Really well marked. No bugs in September, and very few people at this time of year.
I would say this is hard. A lot of up and down. But amazing trail
Great trail. It’s definitely not 7.5 like they say. It’s closer to 9km
Must do great view about halfway through so take the offshoot loop to the view, go through various types of forests and see many beautiful lakes
Highly recommend! If you stop for pictures and water breaks it will likely be longer than 2.5 hours

Lookout point was 100% worth the trek! 8km hike but our app documented 11km—perhaps due to the steep inclines etc.? We were a few unfit people who are excited to have survived the hike. With plenty of rest and a lunch break, we ended up being out there for 7hrs.
Great option of you love hiking but only have a short amount of time in the Algonquin PP.
Beautiful trail through the forest with lakes, rushing rivers and an amazing scenic lookout, after a strenuous hike to said lookout! No bugs, no mud! Be sure to grab an interpretive guide.
Heard a wolf howling at the start of the trail this morning !
Nice trail.

Nice moderate trail. Very long on a hot summer day so pack lots of water. Be careful of wasp nests in the ground as one hiker and her dog got attacked in front of us. The view is nice but very busy. If you want a shorter one with a similar view I recommend booths rock or lookout
Great easy hike. Beautiful view.

Lovely trail in the heart of Algonquin - the trail guide is fantastic because this trail goes through the old historic center of the park so you learn a lot about it as well.  I’d rate it a moderate hike as there are some steep sections.   Great places to sit and enjoy the view, swim, etc.  I’d agree w reviewers that the trail could get very muddy after a rain.  Also, there is a bees nest very close to the trail near Grant Lale on your LHS - watch out for it or go around!   But loved it.

Great trail. We took the guidebook and stopped and read about the history. Made it more interesting for my 14 year old twins. Unfortunately with just over a km left (around post 12) we must have hit a wasps/hornet nest and 3 of 4 of us got stung. Made the last bit a lot faster of a walk to get back to some Benadryl and ice. Ouch. Despite the stings, would definitely recommend!
Very epic

Great trail. Lots of tree roots but wasn't hard. Took our 2.5 year old on the trail and he walked a good amount. Took us 4 hours slow moving with the kiddo. Huge car park. Easy to follow trail. A few mosquitos but nothing some bug spray didn't take care of.
Great trail. Roots. Rock. Water. Cliffs. Views. Rapids . The whole Algonquin experiences

Do no attempt if it has been raining, the mud will make it difficult. Took us over 3:30 to complete in mostly dry weather. Fair amount of people for a Wednesday. Saw chipmunks, frogs but nothing larger. Tons of roots, rocks and ascencions.
Varied interesting beautiful
Great trail - great views & not crowded at all! Slightly longer than the 5 miles expected but still worthwhile

Beautiful trail that I imagine is just as stunning in all seasons. The tough climbs were nicely broken up by flat and downhill patches. Shady too, which was appreciated on a mid-afternoon summer hike.
No dogs :(
Great trail hike with the family
This is a moderate trail. Dry with minimal bugs.  Beautiful hike with a nice view at the look out.
Buggy and rugged.
Such a fantastic trail but be ready to go up and up and up.
Amazon hike!!! Such a beauty view at the time! Pretty x 10!

One of my favorite hikes to date. The trail offered stunning views and a peaceful atmosphere throughout. While labeled as “difficult,” I’d personally rate it moderate—some uneven terrain and steep incline changes make it a bit more of a workout, but still very doable. Bug-wise, it wasn’t too bad; a few mosquitoes and the occasional deer fly, but nothing overwhelming. My dog (Maple) and I started early and wrapped up before the midday heat, which made for a perfect experience. Highly recommend starting early to beat the crowds and enjoy the serenity.
Only a little bit of mud, a few bugs.

We were here in late, July. We didn’t have much mosquito activity only some horseflies. I would still recommend a good bug spray. The dogs got a little muddy and some boggy sections. So I would recommend hiking shoes or some rugged trail running tennis shoes.
Well marked, generally clear. Mix of terrain with straight runs as well as rocky and roots. Overall, lovely trail.
Beautiful trail! Much more difficult than moderate if you are not an avid hiker
Excellent trail, recommended. Well maintained and well marked. Lots of varied terrain and beautiful views. Good shoes and bug spray recommended.
Great trail with amazing views. Lots of roots and rock so be sure to ware appropriate foot gear

Perfect weather today. Cool sunny. Hiked the trail ccw and that was a blessing. The first leg of the hike was wet/muddy. The last leg was beautiful with late afternoon Sun filtering they the forest and much drier (so no muddy shoes in to deal with;) It is a must to take this to the top. Huge payoff view wise. Shdddddd!
not super buggy! quick trail with lots of birds

Incredible hike! Went with 3 Generations (3 Years Old to almost 70) - Took about 3 hours to complete, what a lookout 100% worth the extra walk out! :) 

Wear bug spray, and make sure you have hiking shoes as it’s very rocky / muddy in some sections.
Love the tower portion…if only more of the trail was like that. Rapids also beautiful. Return trip to parking lot is annoying and seemingly never ending with lots of mud.

Great hike and wonderful views at the lookout. With no rain over the past few days, the last two km of the trail are drying out. There are still muddy sections but it is possible to go around them without getting your shoes wet or muddy.
Some areas mucky despite no rain for a few days. Wear proper hiking shoes or shoes you don’t care about getting dirty.
It’s very muddy, we’ve done this hike in the fall before and it was much drier, probably not good time to come here in July
The last couple km were very muddy
Trail was a little muddy but still in great condition.   The view is worth the climb.
Well marked trail. If you are doing the loop I suggest wearing boots because there are many muddy spots. Bugs spray is also a good idea. Pretty forest and great view from the lookout.
Bug spray, and hydrate.  Moderate to advanced fitness level is important

We went midday after the weather calmed from a thunderstorm overnight with rain in the morning. It was plan B (we initially wanted to do Mizzy Lake but based on our research thought Mizzy would be too wet). This trail was also incredibly wet and muddy for about 75% so it was probably a good call to skip Mizzy today. It was still enjoyable though with nice views of the calm lakes, lush mossy forest all around and a well marked trail.  There were some drier patches but be prepared with good boots, as at some points the trail takes you right through some creeks, not all with stable logs/ rocks for stepping. One woman hiking right behind us fell while crossing so be careful with your steps. See photos for how wet and muddy our boots got for reference.  We also completely missed the fork to go up to the lookout peak unfortunately :(
Well marked trail; great condition but not much scenic except one look out.
Great view.  Nice moving water features.  Lots of song birds singing high in the trees.  Wasn't busy for summer.  Some mosquitos to deal with.  Excellent hike.
Well marked but muddy in spots

Very well marked and above average moderate walk. A great trail, we found relatively fewer insects than other routes. A bit muddy towards the end so maybe not good after heavy rain, but look for short mud detours as we could avoid the worst of it. Recommended for a moderate challenge and no need for map due to consistent blue tree markers.
Mudddddy and lots of bugs. The lookout is alright but not worth the mud and bugs maybe better in the fall?
Very muddy many mosquitos but beautiful trail
quiet and muddy but beautiful views
Variety of sceneries from waterfall to gorgeous lookout, moderately challenging trail especially after heavy rainfall, lookout is optional but highly recommended

Excellent well marked path.  Due to recent storm - a few very muddy spots but has rocks and logs to pass over.   (Be prepared to get your boots muddy).  A few downed trees-(from storm) but easily stepped over or around.  The trail has a “shortcut “ for those older folks (me) that were unable to climb the stairs to the view.  It also has a washroom located at post number 11!  This was a 8 km hike - but with the shortcut it was a 5.8km hike.  I was concerned as both hubby and I are seniors and  8 km would have been A LOT.

Several great views of lakes and rapids. Well-marked. 
However I visited 36 hours after a severe storm and the trail contains several downed trees and endless mud.
Very muddy if it has been rained on - bring shoes you are okay with getting wet/dirty.
Quite muddy in some spots. Overall a great hike.
Trail to Tower closed for maintenance June 16-20. Should have had a sign advising this in the parking lot. Not at 3.3 km. Last 1.5 km very muddy to cross creeks.

Side trail to lookout is closed June 16, 2025 to June 20, 2025.

Bring bug spray. Shoutout to the people who let us borrow theirs!

Moderately challenging picking over tree roots a large part of the trail. Well marked. 

A number of wet, muddy creeks on the second half. Look for the different side paths previous hikers chose for a safe way to cross. Always a blue dot trail marker on the other side.
Good! Some mud at the end but otherwise no technical or tough bits
A bit crowded towards the end but the again it’s the weekend.
Big climb up to the Mountain View, tree fallen on the stairs, still mostly usable. Amazing view.
Fun trail, several boardwalks, one big push to the top for a spectacular lookout

Well marked trail with interesting history and few good viewpoints. Muddy at times. Couple good inclines. Lots of bugs. Overall good trail for a good hike.  If you come prepared you'll be fine. Took us 2h17m to do the 8.6km.

Trail is in decent condition. Well worth the trek.  Crews have cleared the downed tree on the stair of it's limbs, very easy to pass. Last km or so is bit muddy but passable, one spot at the end is easy to get off the trail but it's pretty obvious quickly.
Moderate trail, good views!

Fun hike through beautiful pine forest. Nice view at the top but nothing spectacular. Some muddy sections but normal this time of year. Bug repellent needed. Fallen tree has destroyed a small section of the stairs but you can bypass to the right and rejoin the staircase.
The road to the lookout tower was block by a huge pine.
Fun trail, fairly muddy (spring)

Definitely something you’d wanna do in the warmer months. We went in February and it was snowy and rainy. The stairs are quite complicated to climb in the colder months due to snow. Great hike and great views though.
Muddy in the spring & bring bug spray! A great half-day hike.

A large tree has fallen and obstructed the stairs leading to the lookout at station 7. There is a way to climb up but be cautious with the muddy conditions. Bug spray is definitely recommended. Well worth the climb.
There is tree fallen on the stairs and stair case is broken, due to which lookout is very risky to access, please take caution in accessing the top, due to mud the off trail is very slippery
Last 1.5 km quite muddy
get a boot and you are good to go

Lots of tree roots and rocks sticking out on the trail. The trail is very muddy right now. One section of the stairs to the tower has been taken out by a big tree that fell down and crushed the stairs. You can go around tho. Overall the trail is good, the view from the tower is great.
Amazing trail! Very muddy but with good hiking boots and a pole it’s manageable. With recent rainfall the river was flowing fast and high.
Great hike with amazing views. Would love to come back.

Strongly recommend a bathroom stop before this trail! LOL 

Lots of inclines / declines, beautiful views. Wasn’t too crowded, but definitely saw some hikers and their doggos.
Beautiful and well maintained trail! Only issue was the mountain view lookout was blocked by a fallen tree so we couldn’t access the very last part of the climb. Bugs were not bad!

There’s a fallen tree on the stairs…… Super muddy on the trail back.
First part to the look out is NOT nearly as muddy as the other loop side going back- recommend going back the way you came from after the viewpoint. 
Only nice parts are the beginning with the ground lake view & the top view. Rest of hike is in my opinion not worth it based on spring conditions. + bunch of bugs
Watch out for fallen tree onto staircase.
My husband and I and our dog Sophie we hiked the trail  today! We didn't do the stair and lookout part this time! Very muddy in lots of spots! Moderate trail!
Very muddy right now (mid April) but great hike and great views.
Wet trail, lots of navigating around wet spots but overall lots of fun still. Good lookout halfway through for a pit stop. Not too busy this time year.
Great hike but veeery icy!!  Crampons a must to enjoy trail fully.
Still lots of snow on the trail. Much harder than without snow. Glad I wore my cleats and gators.  Quite the workout!
Right now cleats are a must! Trail was lovely and well manicured. View was gorgeous!
very pretty :)
The trail was well maintained. Beautiful and stunning views on the way.  Don't miss the lookout point, it's worth the efforts.
Amazing trial with spectacular scenery all along the hike!  Definitely a  one to do!
Beautiful winter day with a light dusting of fresh snow.
beautiful view, easy to follow trail and well maintained.
Easy to follow the trail. Many great scenic views throughout!
Easy trail to follow good variety of views very quiet this time of year

Years later and All trails still hasn't fixed the length lol. Anyway, great overall conditions on the trail. The snow is well packed. However not only did the current mild temperatures and light rain damper the views at the lookout, they also made the trails slick in spots. If you don't like the sliding feeling on the declines, bring your cramp ons and/or your poles.
Absolutely fantastic views with fresh snow. The entire trail is definitely more than 9kms and with some decent elevation gain at few points.
Last third of the trail is very muddy!
Nice hike today, and (as always) it was longer than listed. About 10kms. Very muddy after the lookout but pleasant.
Trail map slightly inaccurate, different than path and elevation points incorrect.
Too hard.

Definitely not a short trail. Bring a backpack with water and snacks! We didn't bring one and thoroughly regretted it in the end. We were sweaty and tired, but overall a good hike! Lots of rocks and elevation changes, so good footwear required. Also lots of mud this time of year.

Such a great walk, almost 9km for us in the end. Lovely woodland path and paths quiet and very few other walkers. Climbed up to a fantastic viewpoint about halfway through. Fairly boggy and wet towards the end but otherwise fine underfoot.
It was alright, I felt it was a lot of walking in the woods. The look out was the highlight. I feel the Booth's rock trail is a lot better.

A bit too muddy in the end and rain makes it slippery. Hiking shoes help. Great lookout!

2 weeks late for the fall colors peak but still a nice hike.
little muddy, but easy to walk around
Lots of mud but there are small paths around that are slightly muddy. Beautiful lookout though!
Most of the fall colour's are gone already but it's still a worthy view.
One of my favourite trails!
Great Trail with Great views
This is way longer than  I thought

Depending how you go, the first part (or the last)is light-moderate and the stairs are easier than I thought. Second part (or first) is muddy.  Like REALLY muddy, so this is the challenging part. On the other hand, views are spectacular. 
Please note that on weekend it is crowded.
A little muddy. Not too crowded on a Friday.

Have made this hike a half dozen times. First time using Alltrails. While route is well marked, can be helpful to keep on the trail when leaf fall is heavy. The back trail to the parking lot is often wet, including this time even without heavy rains, so good hiking boots are useful. There is a stairs of 133 steps up to the lookout area, so I'd call it moderate difficulty only.

If you’re reading this, it means you’re thinking of doing the trail - Just Do It!!!

Yes. It’s a bit muddy right now. Its Fall. 
Yes. The trail is mainly covered in leaves posing a slip risk. Its Fall. 

Yes. The view is spectacular at the lookout. But I think you got about 3-5 more days before most trees bare all. 

Get outside and enjoy nature. You won’t regret it.

#letsgetlost
Easy to follow trail with beautiful colours throughout. Last quarter of the trail was pretty muddy but manageable. You will get dirty! Definitely worth the hike.

Very muddy on the second half after last night’s rain. Be prepared to go off trail to avoid the deepest mud. Poles were super helpful. View at the top was great. Trail guides available at the start for 50cents.  Nice to know what the numbered markings were for.  Leaves were definitely past peak, but the maples made the forest glow.
Great trail. Beautiful view at the top. Lots of muddy spots close to the end of the trail. Need hiking boots.
Amazing fall colours!
Busy.

Just hiked  Track and Tower Trail in Algonquin Provincial Park last weekend. It's is a must-do hike for any winter enthusiast. The trail itself is 8 KM long, with some moderate inclines. The real beauty of this hike is in the scenery.

In the winter, the trail is blanketed in a thick layer of snow, creating a picturesque winter wonderland. The towering pines, dusted with snow, create an almost fairytale-like atmosphere. The frozen ponds and creeks add to the magic, as they glisten in the winter sunlight.

One of the highlights of the hike is the lookout, which provides breathtaking views of the surrounding forest and lakes. The climb to the top is a bit of a workout, but it is well worth it for the panoramic views.

Overall, the Track and Tower Trail is a fantastic winter hike. The trail is well-maintained, the scenery is breathtaking, and the lookout tower is a must-see. If you are in the area and looking for a winter adventure, this is the hike for you.

If you take the blue trail (only a complete psychopath would take the white trail), the first hour and a half are mildly technical with beautiful woodland scenes, a lake, an amazing waterfall, a few light steps and the reward of a spectacular view. 

The remaining 234 hours it will take you to get through the rest of the trail will make Frodo and Sam’s trip through Mordor seem like a walk in the park. Signage is less frequent and at times, seems to be placed in a way that dares you to find it. At times the trail devolves into swampland where R.O.U.S.s freely roam and feast on the flesh of those who have given up. There are straight routes back, but the “trail” will shun those in favour of making you go up and over a hill, only to make you double back and go up and over the same hill again just for laughs. There are speakers placed at strategic intervals, playing highway sounds so that you think you have almost made it back. You haven’t. Hours later, you will find it deathly quiet again, before hearing the sounds of life once more. Your spirit will be renewed. Just then, you will be passed by European tourists wearing jeans and sneakers that are suspiciously mudless. Take heart. These are merely performers, employed by the park to beat down your spirit and maintain the trail’s fine reputation. 

Eventually you will make it out. When you do, you will already be looking forward to your next visit.

Track and Tower was a great trail that offered a little bit of everything that makes Algonquin Park a special place.

The trail starts out through woodland and features little streams and bridges as well as some great trails that go up and down over the landscape.

As you progress into the trail, you come across lakes (there are quite a few vantage points to the different lakes on the trail) as well as the remnants of old fire towers, tracks, and a bridge. 

Before you get to the tracks and the bridge, you will go through an incredible section featuring a dam with a wooden bridge that goes over it and winds it’s way along the rapids on one side and rock face on another. It seemed to be a popular spot for photographers.

The trail then continues on toward the lookout, which requires some physical endurance as it’s a steep climb followed by a whole lot of stairs. Once up, you can go left to see where the old fire tower was or go right and head straight to the lookout to save yourself some time.

The lookout is really nice — it overlooks a lake where you can see some cabins, etc., as well as the vast forest floor.

The rest of the walk beyond point 10/11 (where the bike trail connects) is a bit boring so be prepared for it to feel a bit long and less dynamic than the first half. It was also incredibly wet and muddy when we went through so dress appropriately!

The hike took us about four hours with tons of stops for photos, snacks, etc.

Only down side is the number of people also on the trail.   Tremendous view.  Daughter and I finished in 2.5 hours.

Great day hike with an amazing view at the summit, especially for sundown. We completed this hike in a group of 7, and started around 6:00pm. At a leisurely pace we made it to post 7 at just over an hour and fifteen minutes. after spending about 45 minutes at the top we descended, with the last half of the loop in the dark. We had no problem staying on the very well marked trail, and the 13 posts throughout the entire loop were great checkpoints. The bugs were bad at the bottom/beginning but as you ascend, they become less of a problem. Would definitely recommend this trail for a great view of Algonquin!
Great Trail, terrain I found rough at times and be prepared to walk up and down 120+ stairs to the lookout. Overall great trip!
Lots of fun. Ups and downs. Stairs! Can u believe they had STAIRS!???. Great time with the kids, and mom!
Excellent trail. Beautiful view at the lookout point. Lots of roots and uneven terrain so have your hiking boots.
Trial is in perfect conditions. Well, of course there are some

Great trail with a variety of terrain... took my friend and I 2.5 hours at a good pace. We enjoyed the views along the way and didn’t rush it. Would recommend lunch at the top as the rocks and views are so worth hanging out for a bit! Wear good shoes as most of the hike is uneven ground with lots of roots. Trail guide mentioned an old railroad although we didn’t see that...

Really lovely trail, definitely moderate in difficulty.  Lots of elevation changes.  As one gentleman said to me about a third of the way in, “You’ll love the stairs!”.  

However, loads of bugs (but what else is to be expected at this time of year?).

The trail is great and moderate in difficulty. There is a portion with lots of steps that you can avoid but I highly recommend it for the view. In total it took us 3 hours but we were a group of 18 so we went a bit slower to keep everyone together. A major downside was all of the mosquitos. Bug spray is a must since I've never seen so many mosquitos in my life.

Really nice trail with some excellent views at ground level and up at the lookout. The terrain is really varied which keeps it interesting. The only downside was the bugs were pretty constant (and persistent) throughout when we went on July 1st. As others have said, the ground is still pretty wet which doesn't help. Bring bug spray, and nets if you want to keep them away from your face!

Really nice trail with waterfalls and lakes and just gorgeous view from the lookout. It would be a great idea to bring some snacks/food and spend some time having lunch at the top and enjoying the view. 
Trail is 4.7 miles (7.7 km) loop trail and marked as moderate. Keep it in mind that it could be very muddy after the rain. 
The park entrance fee is $17 for the vehicle.
first trail run!

Bring lots of bug spray and water.  Had lunch at the top where the tower used to be - was a great spot with little mosquitoes and nice refreshing breeze.  The last quarter of the trail was muddier but still walkable. If you have a walking stick, it will be useful in those muddier spots.
Great variety of scenery during the hike, view at the lookout was worth the trek up! The end of the trail was quite muddy.

Loved this trail! Probably my favourite with centennial ridges. It was challenging but beautiful the whole time! My boyfriend, my dog and I finished this hiked in 2 hour and 20 minutes. Bring water, snacks and bug spray, lots of bugs in some parts but bug spray kept them off us. Muddy parts can be avoided. Loved this hike would definitely hike this one again.
Beautiful trail

The first part through the forest is nice but nothing special. The look of the lake is beautiful but some trees are hiding it. But when you get there the trail gets amazing! Really lovely along the shore kind of but so beautiful! I went at the afternoon and there was still a lot of ice on the trail! Try to go early on a warm day, the tawing ice was making the trail very slippery and it was a little tricky to get around it! Some muddy sections but nothing too bad!

Good condition considering hard pack snow and abundant rain April 20.

lots a good vistas and saw a mama moose with her claf.

amazing trail, lots of historic spots, gorgeous views. The fall colours were amazing, but the stairs were a bit icy that morning up to the old fire tower location. you can still see some of the log chutes in the one pond beneath the surface, the remains of the first cottage hearth is on the trail along woth the old trestle bridge. Not for younger kids.
Amazing winter hike. No need for snowshoes just a good pair of boots. The trail is packed down well, kudos to the people maintaning the trail. We did the full loop in a little over 3 hours.
Came here snowshoeing in the December. Beautiful trail that wasn't very busy. Must go to the top look out to make it worth it. Also saw a moose.

I arrived around 10am on a cold but sunny Saturday in January and the hike was wonderful. I only saw two other people the entire time I was there and they were just heading in as I was heading out. The waterfalls in the winter are amazing, and the lookout was quite nice as well.

Did this trail on a 2 degree day in January. Beautiful hike. Challenging up and downhill and the stairs to the lookout are a good workout. Would love to back in the early fall. It took us 2:45. Though it wasn't icy we wore icers and were glad to have the extra traction on the well trodden snow.
Fantastic views and waterfall, however the trail was quite muddy and hilly making it a little harder then expected. Would definitely visit again.
Amazing trail with lots of waterfalls and lakes and a amazing lookout..wow!!
Walk and learn
Great trail, saw 2 moose!!! Don't walk too fast and check around to see wildlife...

Another great trail. During the fall colour season it would be recommended to start early. The earlier you go the more "privacy" you will have. Not too much fun if you are sharing the vistas with a ton of other people. Weekdays are also better.
Hiking shoes and good physical state would be required for the cache lake lookout. 
Enjoy

Beautiful interpretive trail. Be sure to stop at each sign and read the description from the guide book. Copies can be purchased in advance or picked up at the trail head. Enjoy lunch and a view at the top.

So I did this hike back on March 10, 2018 with my dog. It is an absolutely stunning trail, with several waterfalls. I would highly recommend it, and would definitely do it again! The entire thing took me about 3.5 hours, including a few breaks. 
Advice for winter: this trail was CRAZY icy. I love to hike in solitude, and I went first thing in the morning in winter, so it was totally isolated with nobody else around. But there are several inclines along the trail that, with the snow having melted and re-frozen, were basically giant slides. Luckily nobody was around to watch me grabbing on to tree limbs for support! If you take this trail in the winter, be prepared for ice!
Not a bad hike but large volumes of people on it when we went. A couple very good viewpoints after many stairs.
This hike was fun. Not too buggy and a great view.
Great trail. Terrain was a good mix, steep, flat, rooted ground. The stairs were a nice little workout and we liked the history.
Fabulous trail, a fall must. Gorgeous varied terrain, and always meet lots of Europeans enjoying the trail.

Today is Sunday, June 17, 2018. I arrived at the lookout point about a half hour ago and am embracing the breeze and the escape from the bugs! For all those hiking his today, your welcome for clearing the millions of cobwebs! lol. The hike is generally fairly tame, but the ascent to the lookout point is quite the chore! Especially the never ending staircase!  All in all a good hike, will depart the lookout in just a few minutes for the last half.

This trail is quality for anyone who enjoys a little challenge, with incredible views. I believe it is best hiked in fall or late summer, to keep the bugs fewer and less intrusive. The fall offers stunning views of colourful Canadian forests.
Nice trail and scenic, but VERY muddy may long weekend.
Complete this trail with my wife and dog for 4 hours. Very beautiful view at 7 point. Forgot to open this App as it’s a new one in my iPhone.
Very good for me but my wife had a difficult time. Very muddy in a lot of sections. Lots of rocks and roots.
Gorgeous view! VERY muddy after rain.
Great trail, amazing view!
Great views. A bit muddy after the nights rain but fun
Great hike, marvellous view! A bit muddy today but that's to be expected with the rain.

Beautiful loop along lakes and through classic northern hardwood forest, hiked this mid April and was very icy and flooded, but in the morning there was no one else on the trail. The look out is halfway through and a very nice place for lunch. Highly recommend for families and a moderate length day trip. Took me 3 hours, but could take up to 5.
